claims.text: Older age is a significant independent predictor of severe liver fibrosis in patients with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.
Obesity is a significant independent predictor of severe liver fibrosis in patients with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.
Diabetes mellitus is a significant independent predictor of severe liver fibrosis in patients with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.
An AST/ALT ratio greater than 1 is a significant independent predictor of severe liver fibrosis in patients with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.
Body mass index is the only independent predictor of the degree of fat infiltration in patients with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.
Increased transferrin saturation correlates positively with the severity of hepatic fibrosis in univariate analysis.
Iron studies are not significant predictors of severe liver fibrosis when controlled for age, obesity, diabetes, and AST/ALT ratio.
Gender is not a significant predictor of severe liver fibrosis when controlled for age, obesity, diabetes, and AST/ALT ratio.

evidence.description: In multivariate analysis, older age (P = .001) was a significant predictor of severe liver fibrosis (bridging/cirrhosis).
In multivariate analysis, obesity (P = .002) was a significant predictor of severe liver fibrosis (bridging/cirrhosis).
In multivariate analysis, diabetes mellitus (P = .009) was a significant predictor of severe liver fibrosis (bridging/cirrhosis).
In multivariate analysis, aspartate transaminase/alanine transaminase (AST/ALT) ratio greater than 1 (P = .03) was a significant predictor of severe liver fibrosis.
Body mass index (P = .003) was the only independent predictor of the degree of fat infiltration.
Increased transferrin saturation correlated positively with the severity of fibrosis (P = .02) in univariate analysis.
Iron studies were not significant when controlled for age, obesity, diabetes, and AST/ALT ratio.
Gender was not significant when controlled for age, obesity, diabetes, and AST/ALT ratio.

methodologies.name: Univariate and multivariate analysis of clinical and biochemical variables
methodologies.description: Clinical and biochemical variables were evaluated using univariate and multivariate regression analysis in patients who underwent liver biopsy to identify predictors of severe liver fibrosis.
conditions: liver biopsy performed on all patients

limitations.text: No recognized factors determining increasing fibrosis and histologically advanced disease in NASH prior to this study.
